gloss: to label as; to bill as; to advertise as

forms.label: Past polite
forms.negative: {銘打|めいう}ちませんでした

forms.label: ている past
forms.negative: {銘打|めいう}っていなかった

forms.label: ている past polite
forms.negative: {銘打|めいう}っていませんでした

definitions.gloss: to label as; to bill as; to advertise as
definitions.explanation: To give something a title, label, or description, often for promotional purposes. Frequently implies that the label may be somewhat exaggerated or strategic.

examples.japanese: 「{最終|さいしゅう}セール」と{銘打|めいう}った。
examples.english: It was billed as the 'Final Sale.'

examples.japanese: 「{日本初|にほんはつ}」と{銘打|めいう}った{商品|しょうひん}が{話題|わだい}になった。
examples.english: A product billed as 'Japan's first' became a hot topic.

examples.japanese: {健康|けんこう}に{良|よ}いと{銘打|めいう}ったサプリメントが{数多|かずおお}く{売|う}られている。
examples.english: Many supplements advertised as being good for your health are sold.

examples.japanese: 「{地域|ちいき}{活性化|かっせいか}」と{銘打|めいう}ったイベントが{毎年|まいとし}{開催|かいさい}されている。
examples.english: An event billed as 'regional revitalization' is held every year.

notes:
Literally means "to engrave a name/inscription." In modern usage, it describes labeling or branding something with a particular title or slogan, often for marketing or promotional purposes. The past participle {銘打|めいう}った (labeled as, billed as) is the most common form.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- 「〜」と{銘打|めいう}つ: to bill/label as "~"
- 「〜」と{銘打|めいう}った{商品|しょうひん}: a product labeled as "~"
- 「〜」と{銘打|めいう}ったイベント: an event billed as "~"

REGISTER:
Somewhat formal. Common in news reporting, advertising copy, and written descriptions. In casual speech, 〜と{名付|なづ}けた or 〜と{呼|よ}んだ would be more natural.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {名付|なづ}ける: to name, to call (neutral, no promotional nuance)
- {称|しょう}する: to call oneself, to claim to be (formal, sometimes skeptical)
- {謳|うた}う: to advertise, to promote (similar marketing nuance)
